regime_context: Hong Kong shows a narrow, one-narrative structure: Banks (H + HK) is the sole eligible leader (score 1.188, durability 0.56, breadth 0.462) while everything else ranks below zero or is ineligible. Gate helps on this market's history (validated risk control, no mean-return edge), absorption is low at 0.48, and the dominant leader is mean-reverting with no crowding — so this is a fragile leadership concentration, not a broad trend regime.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Energy (H-shares) clears its absolute-trend gate (eligible flips to true) and narrows the 0.208 score margin against Banks (H + HK) — that two-part condition would retire this watch and mark a potential confirmed leadership handoff.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks is the only eligible theme (trend-gate passed) and leads the rotation by a 0.208 margin over Energy. Durability bar of 0.56 is the highest in the universe, suggesting the leadership has some staying power. However, the theme is unscorable (no ETF proxy), hurst_tag is mean-revert, and breadth of 0.462 is middling — the leadership is real but not broadly confirmed. This is a directional lean on the one confirmed leader, expressed conditionally, not a claim of return edge.
evidence: rotation.leader id = hk_banks, margin 0.208 over challenger
theses.dissent: Hurst tag is mean-revert, meaning the trend has historically reverted rather than persisted; with only one eligible theme and absorption 0.48, leadership is thin and could unwind quickly without a handoff candidate. The mean-revert signature is the strongest bear case against durability.

falsifier.text: Banks (H + HK) loses its eligible status (trend-gate drops below bar) or its score falls below Energy (H-shares) within 20 trading days

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the challenger (rank 2, score 0.98) but is not eligible — it has not passed the absolute-trend gate. Hurst tag is trend, which is encouraging, but durability bar 0.36 is weak and breadth 0.3 is thin. No validated edge supports buying an ineligible challenger before it clears the trend gate. This is an avoid lean on the second name until it demonstrates eligibility.
theses.dissent: Hurst tag is trend (unlike Banks' mean-revert), so if Energy does clear the gate, it could be a more durable leader than Banks. The trend signature is the one reason to keep watching it closely rather than dismissing it outright.
